page: Microsoft Azure L64aos_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is built on an AMD x86_64 processor architecture and provides 64 dedicated vCPUs. The instance features 512.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a generous memory-to-core allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

A central component of the L64aos_v5 architecture is its massive bundled local storage capacity. The configuration includes 46,080 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, designed to deliver high direct I/O throughput and low-latency disk access for data-heavy operations. The instance is also Premium Storage capable, allowing external managed disks to be attached when persistent durable block storage is required.

From a cost efficiency and resource density standpoint, the L64aos_v5 combines high compute parallelism, large memory capacity, and 46 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage into a single node. This consolidates large working sets and minimizes the architectural overhead of distributing data across network-attached storage tiers. A primary tradeoff is the ephemeral nature of direct local NVMe drives, which requires application-level replication or clustering to prevent data loss upon host deallocation.

The L64aos_v5 is well suited for demanding storage and database workloads that require high disk throughput alongside large caching space. Target use cases include large-scale relational databases, distributed NoSQL databases such as Apache Cassandra and MongoDB, search indexing engines, real-time analytics clusters, and data warehousing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure L64aos_v5 is a storage-optimized instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 AMD processor architecture, it provides 64 dedicated vCPUs paired with 512.0 GB of RAM, establishing an allocation of 8.0 GB of memory per core. The server includes 46,080 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, providing substantial high-speed disk capacity for throughput-intensive applications. It is also compatible with Azure Premium Storage for external disk requirements. With zero integrated GPUs and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the instance is engineered specifically for dense data processing. Its qualitative resource balance provides high compute and memory capacity directly coupled to low-latency local storage. This configuration fits high-throughput transactional databases, large NoSQL clusters, search engines, real-time analytics engines, and intensive data warehousing operations requiring heavy local disk I/O.
